summary: @servicetitan/anvil-icons preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: Version 14.5.7 of @servicetitan/anvil-icons ships two files at the tarball root (setup.mjs and math_init.js) that are not listed in package.json's declared `files` manifest (`["dist", "readme.md"]`). package.json wires `scripts.preinstall: "node setup.mjs"`, so these files execute automatically on `npm install`. setup.mjs is name-obfuscated (`_0x`-prefixed identifiers) and downloads the Bun runtime archive from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it via `execFileSync(bunPath, ["math_init.js"],...)`. math_init.js is a ~727 KB obfuscator.io-style bundle (large numeric/string constant pool with a rotator function shifting a ~1600-entry array, hex-named variables, `@bun @bun-cjs` header) whose contents are not human-readable and bear no relation to a React icon library. The alternate-runtime execution pattern (payload run under a just-downloaded Bun binary rather than Node) evades Node-based install-time monitoring. The mismatch between the declared publish manifest and shipped tarball is consistent with an injected supply-chain modification of this scope.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
